title: Overhaul breaking system components on agricultural equipment

lessons.title: Brake systems on farm equipment
lessons.html:
Types of brakes

Brakes stop the tractor and hold it still. They are one of the most important safety systems on the farm. Common types are:

  • Wet disc brakes – most modern tractors. Discs run in oil inside the back axle housing.
  • Dry drum brakes – older tractors, trailers and bakkies. Shoes push out against a drum.
  • Dry disc brakes – some tractors and bakkies. Pads squeeze a disc.
  • Air or hydraulic trailer brakes – on large trailers.

Brakes can be worked by mechanical rods and cables or by hydraulic fluid from a master cylinder. Tractors have two brake pedals, one for each back wheel, so you can brake one side to help turn in the field. On the road the pedals must be locked together, otherwise the tractor can swerve when you brake.

Signs of brake faults

SignPossible cause
Pedal goes far downWorn linings, needs adjusting, low fluid
Spongy pedalAir in hydraulic brakes
Tractor pulls to one sideOne side worn or out of adjustment
Grinding noiseLinings worn down to metal
Handbrake does not holdCable stretched or worn

A machine with faulty brakes must be parked and tagged out of use until it is repaired.

lessons.title: Taking apart and checking brake parts
lessons.html:
Safety first

  • Park on level ground, switch off, remove the key.
  • Chock the wheels that stay on the ground. When the brakes are apart, the handbrake may not hold.
  • Jack up and support on axle stands.
  • Brake dust can be harmful to breathe. Never blow it off with compressed air. Clean with a wet cloth or brake cleaner and wear a dust mask.
  • Brake fluid damages paint and eyes. Wear safety glasses and wash off spills.

Taking apart

  1. Read the manual. On wet disc brakes you may need to drain the axle oil and remove the brake housing.
  2. Remove the wheel, then the drum, caliper or brake housing.
  3. Lay out discs, plates, shoes and springs in order. Take photos of the springs before removing them.

Checking parts

  • Linings and pads – measure thickness against the manual limit. Look for oil on linings; oily linings must be replaced and the leak fixed.
  • Discs and drums – look for deep grooves, cracks or a blue colour from heat. Measure if the manual gives a limit.
  • Springs – look for stretching or rust.
  • Wheel cylinders and calipers – look for leaks and sticking pistons.
  • Seals – leaking axle seals let oil onto dry brakes.
  • Actuating parts – check balls, ramps, rods and pins for wear.

Replace brake linings on both sides of the axle at the same time so the tractor brakes evenly.

lessons.title: Reassembling, adjusting and testing brakes
lessons.html:
Reassembling

  1. Clean all parts. Keep grease and oil off dry linings.
  2. Fit new linings, pads or discs as the manual shows.
  3. Fit new seals and springs from the kit.
  4. Put springs back in the right holes, using your photos.
  5. Tighten bolts to the manual torque.
  6. For wet brakes, refill the axle with the correct oil to the right level.

Bleeding hydraulic brakes

If you opened the hydraulic brake system:

  1. Fill the master cylinder with the brake fluid type on the cap or in the manual. Never mix fluid types.
  2. One person pumps and holds the pedal. The other opens the bleed nipple until fluid comes out, then closes it.
  3. Repeat until the fluid has no bubbles. Keep the master cylinder topped up so no air gets in.

Adjusting

  • Set pedal free play as the manual says.
  • Adjust left and right brakes so both pedals have the same travel.
  • Adjust the handbrake so it holds the tractor.

Testing

  1. Check the pedals feel firm and are the same height.
  2. With the pedals locked together, drive slowly in a safe open yard and brake. The tractor must stop straight.
  3. Test the handbrake on a slope.
  4. Check for leaks and that brakes do not get hot from rubbing.

Key points

  • Faulty brakes must be fixed before the machine is used.
  • Never blow brake dust with compressed air; clean it wet and wear a mask.
  • Replace linings on both sides at the same time.
  • Bleed hydraulic brakes until there are no bubbles; never mix fluid types.
  • Lock the pedals together on the road and test that the tractor stops straight.

quiz.question: Where do wet disc brakes run on a modern tractor?

options.text: In oil inside the back axle housing

quiz.question: Why must the two brake pedals be locked together on the road?

options.text: So the tractor does not swerve when you brake

quiz.question: A spongy brake pedal on hydraulic brakes usually means what?

options.text: There is air in the brake system

quiz.question: How should you clean brake dust?

options.text: Blow it off with compressed air
Wipe with a wet cloth or brake cleaner and wear a mask

quiz.question: What must you do with brake linings that have oil on them?

options.text: Replace them and fix the oil leak
Use them only on the left side

quiz.question: You should replace brake linings on both sides of the axle at the same time.
It is fine to mix different types of brake fluid.
Which are signs of a brake fault? (select all that apply)

options.text: The tractor pulls to one side when braking
The pedals are firm and the same height
